verdict.rationale: Vast.ai documents interruptible instances as a first-party instance type. They are bid-based, low priority, and often 50%+ cheaper than on-demand, and the docs state they "may be paused", which gives basic preemption semantics. The docs in the pack do not spell out the preemption mechanics in depth. Missing for 10: detailed preemption semantics (what triggers a pause on outbid, any notice or grace period, resume behavior, data and disk state while paused, billing during a pause), and independent or hands-on corroboration of interruptible behavior.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can rent spot or interruptible GPU capacity at a deep discount with clearly documented preemption semantics

citations.quote: Interruptible instances use a bidding system: **Lowest cost** (often 50%+ cheaper than on-demand)
Interruptible: Low Priority. Lowest cost, may be paused
Vast.ai offers three instance types with different priority levels and pricing models to match your workload requirements and budget.
